paragraphs.text: Countries with many wind farms face a simple question: what happens on a still day? In one northern country, output from wind can fall from half of national demand to almost nothing within twelve hours.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Storage helps only a little. Batteries are good for minutes and hours, not for the week-long calm spells that occur two or three times each winter, and pumped-storage lakes are limited by geography.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The usual answer is a mix. Gas plants that run for a few days a year, imports through undersea cables, and factories that agree to pause production all cost money, but together they cover the gap.
paragraphs.label: C
